mpsc-udc-efcc-2018-paper-1-d07.question:
Do as directed:                                                                              **(10×2=20)**
(a) alike that it is difficult/ the two sisters look so/ to tell one from the other (rearrange to make meaningful sentence)
(b) He has black dog and white bitch; inner and outer wall were both strongly defended. (insert
Articles)
(c) Walk __quickly, else__ you will not overtake him. (identify the part of speech of the underlined words)
(d) He likes to be called ‘Sir. (change the voice)
(e) I am too weak to walk. (Rewrite using ‘so’ instead of ‘too’)
(f) Lively is to ____ **(1)** as loyal is to _____ **(2)** (insert 1- animated/ genuine & 2- prudent/ devoted)
(g) The bank ____every day at 9 a.m. and ____ at 3 p.m. (insert appropriate forms of ‘open/ close’)
(h) The boy is very fat. He cannot run. (combine into a simple sentence using infinitive)
(i) I am his friend. (change to negative)
(j) She is a __singer by profession__. (substitute an adjective for the underlined)
mpsc-udc-efcc-2018-paper-1-d07.explanation: Independent study guide: Follow each specific task and preserve its meaning. Part(d) embeds a passive infinitive, not a fully passive main clause; the sample makes its agent explicit. Part(i) needs an antonym-based equivalent, not simple negation reversing the statement.
answers: (a) The two sisters look so alike that it is difficult to tell one from the other. (b) He has a black dog and a white bitch; the inner and outer wall were both strongly defended (retain the printed singular wall/coordination defect; walls may be intended). (c) quickly: adverb; else: conjunction meaning otherwise. (d) He likes people to call him “Sir” (active equivalent of the passive infinitive). (e) I am so weak that I cannot walk. (f) animated; devoted. (g) opens; closes. (h) The boy is too fat to run. (i) I am not his enemy. (j) She is a professional singer.

mpsc-asst-2010-paper-1-d05.question:
Use the correct tense of the verbs:                                                   **(10×1=10)**
(a) The farmer _______ (cut) the corn which _______ (ripe)
(b) He _______ (sleep) when we _______ (arrive).
(c) John _______ (drink) coffee every morning.
(d) I _______ (go) home next Sunday.
(e) To err _______ (be) human.
(f) He _______ (give) her a book which she _______ (refuse) to read.
(g) All parents _______ (love) their children.
mpsc-asst-2010-paper-1-d05.explanation: Independent study guide: Use time and aspect cues; some source clauses lack a tense cue and therefore accept coherent alternatives. The source treats ripe as a verb, but in ordinary use it is an adjective, requiring a supplied be or the related verb ripen.
answers: (a) The farmer cut the corn which was ripe (or had ripened; this resolves the defective verb cue, not a uniquely scored form). (b) was sleeping; arrived. (c) drinks. (d) will go/am going, both future reference. (e) is. (f) gave; refused is one coherent past narrative, while gives/refuses is a possible present habitual reading. (g) love.
